metadata.title: Cage, Rules, Belts.
metadata.purpose: A viewer who follows neither sport can tell MMA from boxing in one glance, and explain why 'world champion' means one name in MMA and up to four in boxing.
metadata.register: Teardown (adapted for newcomers — every term is defined on first use)
metadata.audience: Viewers new to combat sports: no assumed knowledge of cages, weight classes, sanctioning bodies, or submissions.
metadata.color_semantics: claude fidelity palette; one terracotta moment per beat. The accent always marks the side of the comparison the beat is arguing about — the cage in B01, the six MMA weapons in B02, the four sanctioning bodies in B04, the vacant belt in B05.
deviations: IN-FOR-BEAR LAW dropped: the host is Param Madan, so no 'in for Bear' sign-off appears.
OUTRO-LOCK not applied: the @NikBearBrown card is replaced by MvbOutro carrying the host's name (user decision, matching worldcup-2026-twenty-shots).
folderLabel is the host's name rather than a channel handle — no handle was supplied and none was invented.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW reel: the Claude UI appears only at B00 (ask) and B08 (handoff). B00B-B07 are concept illustrations in scenes/MmaVsBoxing.tsx. Manim is not installed and is not needed — no equation beats. Every belt holder on screen is a prop, ledgered in SOURCES.md with a retrieval date, because these expire.

beats.new_visual_element: Claude composer — the ask lands answered
beats.narration_text: Hey, this is Param Madan, and this explainer video is on M M A versus boxing, and who the world champions actually are. Quick question. Who is the world champion of M M A boxing? It's a trick question. There is no such thing. They are two different sports, with different rules, different arenas, and very different answers to who is on top.

show.event: cold open on the Claude composer, cream page, greeting above the card
the ask types itself into the composer
three output lines print — the shape of the whole reel

props.command: I don't follow combat sports. Explain the difference between MMA and boxing, and tell me who the world champion is in each.
output: MMA: a cage, six weapons, one organization
Boxing: a ring, fists only, four organizations
So 'world champion' means two different things

beats.new_visual_element: the promise card — the three questions the reel will answer
beats.narration_text: So here's what this video is, and why it's worth three minutes. Three questions tell these two sports apart: what the floor looks like, what a fighter is allowed to do, and how many belts are on the line. Answer those three and you will never confuse them again. You don't need to follow either sport — nothing here is assumed.

show.event: eyebrow WHAT THIS VIDEO IS above the serif headline
a tile rises: cage or ring, one weapon or six, one belt or four
the promise strip lands under a terracotta rule

props.headline: Three questions tell the two sports apart.

beats.new_visual_element: the floor plan — octagon against square ring
beats.narration_text: Start with the fastest tell: the floor plan. M M A happens inside a cage with eight sides, called the octagon. Boxing happens in a square ring, bounded by ropes. Cage means M M A. Ropes mean boxing. That one glance never lies.

show.event: the octagon draws in terracotta
the roped square draws beside it in ink
the rule lands under a terracotta strip

beats.narration_text: Now the rules. Boxing is punches only, above the belt, on your feet. That is the entire toolkit — one weapon. M M A stands for mixed martial arts, and mixed is the whole point: punches, kicks, knees, elbows, takedowns, and submission holds like chokes and arm bars. Six. And when a boxer goes down, the action stops. When an M M A fight hits the floor, it is often just getting started.

show.event: the boxing row resolves to a single chip and the numeral 1
a chip lands in terracotta, six in all
the floor rule lands

beats.new_visual_element: MMA's answer — one organization, twelve divisions
beats.narration_text: So who is the champion? In M M A, one organization runs the top of the sport: the U F C. Twelve weight divisions, and one champion in each. Take the heavyweights. The U F C heavyweight champion is Tom Aspinall, from England. One division, one belt, one name. There is a wrinkle — heavyweight also has an interim champion right now, Ciryl Gane, standing in while Aspinall is out. But that is one organization managing itself, not a rival league.

show.event: the UFC card lands in terracotta
two tiles rise: 12 divisions, 1 champion each
the heavyweight line resolves to the champion's name
the interim-title caveat lands in the strip

props.note: Heavyweight also has an interim champion, Ciryl Gane — a stand-in while the champion is out, not a rival organization.

beats.narration_text: Boxing is messier. There is no single boxing league. Four separate organizations each award their own world title: the W B C, the W B A, the I B F, and the W B O. So one weight class can have four champions at the same time. When a single fighter wins all four, they are called undisputed.

show.event: a terracotta card lands: WBC, WBA, IBF, WBO

show.at: on 'four champions at the same time'
show.event: the consequence line resolves
the definition lands in the strip

beats.new_visual_element: the heavyweight ledger — four belts, three names, one vacancy
beats.narration_text: Here is the proof, live right now. Boxing's heavyweight belts are split. Agit Kabayel holds the W B C title. Murat Gassiev holds the W B A. Daniel Dubois holds the W B O. And the I B F belt is sitting vacant. Four belts, three champions, one empty seat — in the same weight class where M M A has essentially one name.

show.event: a ledger row draws in: organization, then holder
the IBF row lands in terracotta italic
the count resolves beneath the ledger

beats.new_visual_element: undisputed — all four belts, one name
beats.narration_text: Undisputed is rare, and that is the point. In men's boxing today, exactly one fighter holds all four belts in his division: Naoya Inoue, at super bantamweight. In the U F C, holding the only belt in your division is simply what being champion means.

show.event: the four abbreviations line up in terracotta
the name lands at poster scale
the contrast lands in the strip

beats.narration_text: So here is your test. What is the floor — cage or ring? What is legal — fists only, or fists, feet, knees and grappling? And how many belts — one per division, or up to four floating around? Answer those three and you can read either sport. One warning: the names on the belts change every few months. The structure does not.

show.event: a card lands with the question and its two answers
the warning lands in the strip

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt: pick a weight class in boxing and list who holds each of the four major belts today, then explain what would have to happen for one fighter to unify them. Run it on any sport with more than one governing body. What you are looking for is how the structure of a sport decides who gets called the best.

show.event: the composer returns, greeting reads 'Your turn.'
the prompt types itself in
